2607.03744.title: Can Conversational Temporal Dynamics Improve Depression Detection in Dyads? A Preliminary Investigation in Multi-Modality Perspectives
2607.03744.paper_summary: Automatic depression detection from clinical interviews typically models the semantic content and acoustic characteristics of participant speech. However, the interactional timing between the clinician and participant remains comparatively under-modeled. We investigate conversational temporal dynamics, specifically dyadic turn-pair timing, as a primary modality fused with self-supervised encoders. Evaluated on the DAIC-WOZ dataset, we compare a compact 24-dimensional timing module against frozen WavLM-large and RoBERTa-large baseline detectors. This temporal module achieves the highest single-modality performance on the development set. Furthermore, a convex-weighted late fusion strategy improves overall performance to 0.804 and 0.669 macro-F1 on the development and test sets, respectively. The learned fusion effectively assigns zero weight to acoustics, demonstrating that conversational timing serves as a lightweight, interpretable complement for dyadic depression screening.
2607.03744.paper_summary_zh: 自動抑鬱症檢測通常從臨床訪談中建模參與者語音的語義內容和聲學特徵。<lb/>然而，臨床醫生與參與者之間的互動時機仍然相對未被充分建模。<lb/>我們研究對話的時間動態，特別是雙方輪流發言的時機，作為與自我監督編碼器融合的主要模式。<lb/>在DAIC-WOZ數據集上進行評估，我們將一個緊湊的24維時間模塊與凍結的WavLM-large和RoBERTa-large基準檢測器進行比較。<lb/>這個時間模塊在開發集上達到了最高的單一模態性能。<lb/>此外，一種凸加權的後期融合策略將整體性能提升至0.804和0.669的宏觀F1分數，分別在開發集和測試集上。<lb/>所學的融合有效地將聲學的權重設置為零，顯示出對話時機作為雙方抑鬱篩查的輕量級、可解釋的補充。
